📚 Today you learned

Fractional Share Execution

In forex you trade in lots; in US equities your broker can slice a single share into decimals. Your 0.3 GOOG and 0.5 SPXC aren't rounding artifacts — IBKR internally fills a fractional order against its own inventory or nets it across clients, since exchanges only trade whole shares. The catch: fractional shares usually can't be used to place a limit/stop order directly on the exchange book the way a whole share can in every venue — IBKR routes it through its fractional trading desk at the NBBO, which is why your fills have historically landed a few cents off the quoted price (GOOG filled $364.83 against a $365 limit). It also means in a true liquidity crunch, fractional positions may be harder to exit cleanly than round lots — one more reason position-sizing math should assume slightly worse fills than the whole-share theoretical price.

Also today: Odd lot — any order under 100 shares (the old exchange round-lot size); most retail orders are odd lots and get slightly different print-reporting treatment on the tape.
